title: CAP: A General Purpose Computation-in-memory with Content Addressable Processing Paradigm
problem: Conventional CAM-based CIM accelerators are limited to vector-vector operations only and require lengthy sequences of search-update iterations. Current computation-in-memory approaches cannot efficiently support general-purpose computation patterns.
motivation: Computation-in-memory using CAM can overcome memory wall bottlenecks through in-situ processing, but existing implementations lack generality and efficiency.
method: CAP performs general-purpose computations by chaining search-and-update operations on content-addressable memory (hardware that finds data by looking up its value rather than address). All computation happens in the memory itself—avoiding the slowness of shuttling data back and forth to a separate processor. This generalizes earlier CAM-based systems, which could only perform vector multiplication.
key_novelty: CAP extends CAM-based computation-in-memory from vector-only operations to general-purpose computing through optimized search-and-update sequences.
contributions: General-purpose computation-in-memory architecture using content addressable processing
Overcomes vector-vector operation limitation of conventional CAM-based CIM
Optimized search-update operation sequences for broader functional support
CAP paradigm enabling efficient in-situ computing under memory wall constraints
limitations: Limitations not discussed in provided abstract.
primary_theme: Content addressable processing for general-purpose in-memory computing
